result:
Nothing in `ces-revisions` works end to end yet: the package is a greeting `main()` with two smoke tests. So I'm staging this as a new project. There is no spec, so the outcomes below are candidates drawn from your brief, `specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md`, with the three research files as background for facts and costs. None of them is confirmed until you say so.

## Candidate outcomes (unranked)

All are from `ces-revisions-prompt.md`.

| # | Outcome: what you get | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|
| O1 | Revision series and their dispersion over time for each of the four stages (1st→2nd, 2nd→3rd, 3rd→benchmark, post-benchmark/wedge-back), total nonfarm, SA | Small data volume, likely MB-scale (monthly national series × vintages). Usable vintage depth is measured by its core stage. The FRED/ALFRED API allows 120 requests/min, and the BLS API v2 allows 500 queries/day with 50 series per query (published limits, to verify). |
| O2 | The same per-stage dispersion history by NAICS supersector | Depends on supersector vintage coverage, which is thinner than for total nonfarm. Measured by its core stage. |
| O3 | Split of the one- and two-month SA revision into an NSA-sample part and a seasonal-factor part | Needs paired NSA and SA vintages. All three research files say no long-run published decomposition exists. The data cost is near O1's. |
| O4 | Effect of collection interval and first-closing rate on the scale of the one-month revision | The calendar-derived interval is cheap. Collection-rate history may need hand-collection from archived releases. Measured by its core stage. |
| O5 | A hand-built covariate set: real BLS appropriations, CRs/shutdowns/sequestration, FTE, CES sample size | Your time is the main cost: roughly 40+ fiscal years of budget justifications and FedScope extracts. The per-year cost is measured by its core stage. |
| O6 | Shrinkage estimates of how funding, staffing and sample size relate to revision scale, descriptive and not causal | Compute can't be estimated without a fit, and it depends on O5 existing. |
| O7 | News-vs-noise decomposition across all four stages, with a latent true path and the benchmark as an irregular, higher-precision observation | NUTS compute is unknown until one fit runs. Marginalizing the state with Dynamax is the main lever. Measured by its core stage. |

**Later qualities.** These are not outcomes, so I'll place them in later stages or Ranked-list items:
- vintage manifests and point-in-time storage
- the full validation suite (prior predictive checks, PPC on dispersion, LOO vs a constant-variance baseline, pseudo-real-time checks)
- supersector partial pooling beyond the first working fit
- structural-change handling for 2003 and 2020–22

## Proposed tracks

- **A: Revision-scale measurement (O1, O2).** I propose a known progression: acquire vintages, compute the stage series, then add supersectors. Every other track consumes it.
- **B: Seasonal vs. sample (O3).** Research. It is split from C and D because its answer stands whether or not collection timing or funding matters.
- **C: Collection interval (O4).** Research. It is split from D because it is identified off sharp within-year variation, while D's covariates are slow and collinear. Either answer stands alone.
- **D: Operational capacity (O5, O6).** Research. O5 is mostly your hand-work, and O6 can't start without it.
- **E: Multi-vintage state-space model (O7).** Research. The brief's Part C bundles B, C and D into this one model. I've split them because a joint model would make each driver's answer wait on the full machinery. E can absorb their findings later as covariates.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14 via uv, from `.python-version` and `uv.lock`.
- NumPyro (NUTS), Dynamax, ArviZ and Polars, from the brief. One caveat: JAX wheels for 3.14 need checking before any modeling stage.

## Proposed name

`ces-revisions`, giving `specs/ces-revisions-roadmap.md`. No file by that name exists.

**One request:** please rank the outcomes within each track and the tracks among themselves, and confirm or change the tracks, their kinds (especially A as a known progression), and the name.

Optionally, I can first run one small probe: count the available ALFRED vintages for total nonfarm SA and NSA and one supersector, to firm up the O1/O2/O3 cost notes. I'll only run it if you say yes.
